newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - May 27.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - May 27.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- At least 30 people were killed after torrential rains lashed across the northern part of the Philippines (MANILA BULLETIN)

- Philippine President Fidel Ramos assures Central Luzon residents that the dike built to block lahar is still intact and the breached portions can be reapired in two days. (PHILIPPINE DAILY INQUIRER)
- Three political events were cancelled as tropical depression lashed Manila. (MANILA TIMES)
- Lippo Bank of Indonesia is now considering buying into a thrift bank, Prime Savings Bank, after failing to take over Monte de Piedad & Savings Bank (BUSINESS DAILY)
- Torrential rains and the cancellation of the business in the Philippine Clearing House prompted the Philippine Stock Exchange to suspend trading after a slow session.
- The National Power Corp is reducing its rates on industrial customers in Luzon by 4.8 centavo per kilowatt-hour.
- Mabuhay Philippines Satellite Corp can now provide broadcast services through its Agila II satellite after the consortium got the go-ahead from the Japanese government (MANILA TIMES)
